content.comment_body: I recently upgraded my [product_name] [version_no] to [version_no]. When I work with the installed modules ([article_no]), I am required to manually choose the USB PC cable option during each interaction. For tasks like uploading a new program version, I must select USB multiple times to stop the module, upload the program, and start it again, because the system keeps reverting to Ethernet as the default. Is there a way to set a preferred or default connection method? I would find it helpful to set this once per installation or per project, rather than having to select it every time. If the feature doesn't exist in the current [version_no], perhaps it could be added in a future update.
I'm also interested in having this feature. It would be valuable to change the default connection method to something other than Ethernet.

It's not ideal that [company_name] set [product_name] [article_no] to default to Ethernet, and apparently that's mandatory. I've already contacted [company_name] about this issue; ideally, [product_name] [version_no] and earlier would connect via cable, while [product_name] [version_no] would use Ethernet. Hopefully, [company_name] will address this in a future update. There are other minor issues too, like property screens sometimes being too large so the OK button is out of view. When editing a PI regulator block, you may need to move the properties window up to access the OK and Cancel buttons. This occurs every time with PI regulators.

analysis.insight_summary: Users find it inconvenient that [product_name] [version_no] always defaults to Ethernet as the connection method. This requires manual selection of USB for every interaction with [product_name] [version_no] modules, which disrupts workflow efficiency, especially for routine actions like stopping, uploading, and starting modules. Some users also mentioned UI issues, such as overly large property windows that obscure important controls.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to allow setting a default or preferred communication method (like USB), reducing repetitive manual selection and providing a smoother workflow when working with compatible hardware modules.
